yaml.description-meta: Graduate course on the economics of crime, University of São Paulo (FEA-USP).

markdown.markdown:
::: {.site} ```{=html}
Economics of Crime I

EAE6089 · Graduate

Department of Economics, School of Economics, Business and Accounting (FEA-USP)

Danilo Souza · Third term, 2026

``` ```{=html}
Lecture plan Reading list Office hours Email ← All courses
``` ::: {#description .sec} Organised around topics, this course — together with its sequel, Economics of Crime II — aims to equip students to read and critically evaluate the literature on the economics of crime, with an emphasis on empirical work using modern causal identification strategies. We discuss central questions in the field: the effects of policing and the structure of punishment on criminal behaviour, the consequences of immigration, the effectiveness of public policy in illegal markets, and the dynamics of organised crime. Beyond becoming familiar with the core literature, students will learn to recognise the limits of existing evidence, identify open questions, and propose original research. ::: ::: {#meetings .sec} ## Meetings ::: {.info-block} [Room]{.info-label} [A-8, FEA-1]{.info-value} [Time]{.info-label} [Mondays and Thursdays, 4:00–5:50 pm]{.info-value} [Term]{.info-label} [Third term, 2026]{.info-value} ::: ::: ::: {#assessment .sec} ## Assessment ::: {.info-block} [20%]{.info-label} [Referee report on an unpublished paper]{.info-value} [20%]{.info-label} [Presentation of a published paper]{.info-value} [60%]{.info-label} [Research project: presentation and final paper]{.info-value} ::: ### Key dates {.subhead} ::: {.info-block} [26 Aug]{.info-label} [Referee report due]{.info-value} [23 & 28 Sep]{.info-label} [Research project presentations]{.info-value} [9 Oct]{.info-label} [Final research project due]{.info-value} ::: ::: ::: {#syllabus .sec} ## Syllabus ::: {.topics} 1. Motivation: data, the state of the field, and empirical challenges 2. The rational choice model: static and dynamic 3. Police presence, enforcement, and discrimination in policing 4. Incarceration, monitoring, and punishment 5. Labour market conditions and education 6. Economic shocks and general equilibrium effects 7. Organised crime: causes and consequences ::: A detailed reading list for each topic is available [here](../files/reading-list.pdf){.pub-link}. ::: ::: {#readings .sec} ## Main references ::: {.readings} Lecture notes · Danilo Souza Buonanno, P., P. Vanin, and J. Vargas (2022). *A Modern Guide to the Economics of Crime*. Edward Elgar Publishing. Chalfin, A. and J. McCrary (2017). Criminal deterrence: a review of the literature. *Journal of Economic Literature* 55(1), 5–48. Draca, M. and S. Machin (2015). Crime and economic incentives. *Annual Review of Economics* 7, 389–408. Cook, P. J., S. Machin, O. Marie, and G. Mastrobuoni (2013). *Lessons from the Economics of Crime: What Reduces Offending?* MIT Press. Benson, B. and P. R. Zimmerman (2010). *Handbook on the Economics of Crime*. Edward Elgar Publishing. ::: Selected journal articles are assigned for each topic. ::: ::: {#course-contact .sec} ## Questions Questions that come up during class are best resolved in class. For anything that remains, please come to office hours. Short questions — ones that fit in a few lines — can be sent by email with the subject line `EAE6089 — FirstnameLastname`. Beyond that, feel free to reach out in person or by email about anything else. ::: {.contact-info} [Office hours: book a slot](https://calendly.com/) · Room 221, FEA-2 [danilosouza@usp.br](mailto:danilosouza@usp.br) ::: ::: [© 2026 Danilo Souza · [Back to homepage](../index.html)]{.footer-note} :::
